fullDescription: A restaurant website landing page built around one working control: the seating time you pick rewrites tonight's menu. Four seating blocks sit at the top of the page, one of them hatched out because it is full, and choosing a time strikes through every dish the kitchen cannot serve at that service, each with the real reason printed next to it. Pure CSS, no JavaScript, using radio inputs and :checked sibling selectors. Deep forest green ground, cream type, tan prices, a slab serif that reads like a neighbourhood dining room rather than a template. Reusable for any restaurant, wine bar, supper club or booking page, and the picker pattern transposes to any list that changes with a selected option.

structured.summary: A LANDING PAGE for a small independent restaurant, whose entire point of view is that AVAILABILITY IS THE DESIGN rather than a footnote: the SEATING YOU PICK REWRITES TONIGHT'S MENU. Build it as a real working control with NO JavaScript: four `<input type="radio" name="seating">` elements (17:45, 18:30, 20:00, 20:45) placed as siblings ahead of the menu, visually hidden, driving everything through `:checked ~` sibling selectors, with 20:00 checked by default so a static render already shows the mechanic working. GROUND: deep forest green #2b3a2e across the whole page, flat, no gradient and no texture anywhere. Type: warm cream #ddd5c7, prices in tan #a68a6a, secondary copy in pale sage #b9c4b4, and the brightest cream #f7f4e4 reserved for the booking buttons so the primary action is the brightest object on the page. STRUCTURE, top to bottom. (1) A slim sticky nav: wordmark, three text links (Tonight / The room / Find us), and a solid cream 'Book a table' button. (2) A deliberately SMALL masthead, so the control outweighs it: the restaurant name in a heavy slab serif at about 92px, one plain sentence beneath it ('Twelve tables around an open kitchen'), and tonight's date ranged right. NO hero banner, no headline describing the idea, no photograph, no gradient band. (3) THE CONTROL, immediately: a plain heading reading 'Pick a seating' and four large FILLED blocks side by side, each carrying the time at about 44px in the slab face over a small bold uppercase status line ('First service', 'Second service, 2 seats', 'Late service'). The selected block is a solid cream fill with dark green type. One block is FULL: filled with a loud 45-degree sage hatch, its numerals struck through and set on a small solid backing so they stay readable, its input `disabled` so it cannot be chosen. Beneath the blocks, a solid cream booking button whose label NAMES the selected seating ('Book the 20:00 seating') and a quiet 'or call' line. (4) TONIGHT'S LIST, already written for the selected seating: a heading that also names the seating ('Cooking at 20:00'), then three courses (To start / To follow / To finish) of dish rows, each a dish name in the slab face with one line of ingredients beneath and the price ranged right in tan. Any dish the kitchen cannot serve at the selected seating is STRUCK THROUGH in sage, dimmed, and carries a solid sage TAG next to it naming the constraint ('Late service only'), and its price is struck too. Unavailable dishes are never hidden, because seeing what you are missing is the point. (5) A CREAM #f7f4e4 band with dark green type for 'The room': two short paragraphs and a small right-hand column of labelled facts (Tables / Service charge / Open). (6) A two-column block (deliberately not a symmetrical three-up) for the wine pairing price and the allergy policy. (7) 'Find us': address, seating times, phone at large size, and a final cream 'Book a table' button. (8) A single-line footer. Fully responsive, fluid widths, works at 390px and 1440px, and the page scrolls with real sections. Invent the restaurant, never name a real one.

style.description: A neighbourhood dining-room register rather than a fine-dining one, which is the whole reason it does not read as generated. The palette is earthy and measured: a deep forest green #2b3a2e ground carrying about 80 percent of the page area, warm cream #ddd5c7 type, tan #a68a6a for prices and rules, sage #8a9a7e for anything unavailable, and the brightest cream #f7f4e4 held back for the booking buttons alone. No gradients, no glass, no blur, no shadows, no paper texture, no dot-grid, and no photography at all. The type does the register work: a sturdy slab serif (Zilla Slab) set in SENTENCE CASE for the wordmark, the section heads and the dish names, with a plain grotesque (Karla) for prose. Uppercase letter-spaced micro-labels are rationed to four on the entire page, because a page full of them is a template fingerprint. Rules are 2px rather than hairlines, and the seating blocks are filled rather than outlined, so the page keeps real mass at thumbnail size. The only texture on the page is the hatch on the full seating, and it earns its place by being the one thing you cannot have.
style.prompt: Design on a FLAT deep forest green #2b3a2e ground with no gradient, glass, blur, shadow, paper texture, dot-grid or photograph anywhere. Set type in warm cream #ddd5c7, prices and rules in tan #a68a6a, secondary copy in pale sage #b9c4b4, and reserve the brightest cream #f7f4e4 for the booking buttons and one full-width light band so the primary action is always the brightest object on the page. Use a sturdy SLAB SERIF (Zilla Slab, 600 and 700) in SENTENCE CASE for the wordmark, section heads and dish names, and a plain grotesque (Karla) for prose. Use at most four uppercase letter-spaced labels on the whole page. Draw 2px rules, not hairlines, and fill the seating blocks rather than outlining them. Do NOT use a high-contrast Didone, do NOT letter-space the wordmark, and do NOT set a fine-dining register: that combination is the default generated restaurant page. No centered headline over a glow band, no decorative pill row, no symmetrical three-up trust strip, no logo marquee, no invented statistics, no fake press quotes, no emoji, no em-dashes in visible copy.

layout_and_structure.description: A scrolling landing page that opens on its own mechanic instead of announcing it. A slim sticky nav, a small masthead, then the seating control as the loudest thing above the fold, then the menu already filtered to the selected seating, then a cream room band, a two-column terms block, a find-us block with the final CTA, and a one-line footer. One content width, everything left-aligned to a single origin. On mobile the seating blocks wrap to two per row and every section stacks.

prompts.prompt: Build a slim sticky nav on the page ground with a 2px tan bottom rule: the restaurant name in the slab face bold at the left, three plain text links (Tonight, The room, Find us) that hide below the medium breakpoint, and a solid cream button reading 'Book a table' at the right. Then a deliberately small masthead: the restaurant name as an h1 in the slab face at clamp(46px, 7vw, 92px), sentence case, tight letter-spacing, in the brightest cream, with one plain sentence beneath it in pale sage ('Twelve tables around an open kitchen. Barkly Place, Fitzroy.') and tonight's date ranged right in tan. Scope the wordmark's font-size to a class with !important, because a host stylesheet can override a bare h1. Do not add a tagline that explains the site, a hero image, a gradient band or a decorative pill row.

Place four `<input type="radio" name="seating">` elements with ids s1745, s1830, s2000 and s2045 as SIBLINGS immediately ahead of both the selector row and the menu, visually hidden with an sr-only class, with s2000 `checked` and s1830 `disabled`. Under a plain slab heading reading 'Pick a seating', lay four `<label>` blocks in a flex row that wraps, each `flex: 1 1 150px`, filled with a darkened green #222e25, a 2px tan border, and 18px of padding, holding the time at clamp(30px, 4.4vw, 44px) in the slab face over a small bold uppercase status line. Style the selected block with `#sXXXX:checked ~ .selector-row label[for="sXXXX"]` (a sibling combinator from the input to the row, NOT an adjacent one, since the inputs are not next to the labels): solid cream fill, dark green type, cream border. Give the full seating a 45-degree `repeating-linear-gradient` hatch in sage over the dark green, a sage border, `cursor: not-allowed`, and put its numerals and its 'Full' label on small solid dark backings so they stay readable through the hatch. Beneath the blocks, a solid cream booking button and a quiet 'or call' line.

prompts.part: The menu that the control rewrites
prompts.partPt: The menu that the control rewrites
prompts.prompt: After the control, a 2px tan rule, then a heading naming the selected seating ('Cooking at 20:00') with 'Kitchen closes 22:30' ranged right. Then three courses (To start, To follow, To finish), each a small slab heading in tan over a stack of dish rows. Each row is a flex row: on the left the dish name in the slab face at 20px in cream plus one line of ingredients in pale sage beneath, on the right the price in tan in the slab face. Do NOT put a dotted leader between the dish and the price. Tag the constrained rows with a service class (for example `late-only`, `second-service`) and write the strike rules as `#s1745:checked ~ .menu-section .late-only .dish-name { color: sage; text-decoration: line-through; text-decoration-thickness: 2px; }`, striking the price too and dimming the ingredient line. Constrain the menu to a readable measure of about 820px so the price does not float half a screen away from the dish.

prompts.part: The room, the terms, and find us
prompts.partPt: The room, the terms, and find us
prompts.prompt: A full-width band in the light cream with dark green type headed 'The room': a 1.2fr/1fr grid with two short specific paragraphs on the left (what the building was, how the kitchen works) and a small right-hand column of three labelled facts, each a bold uppercase label with the value ranged right over a 2px rule (Tables / Service charge / Open). Then back on the green ground, a TWO-column block (not three, a symmetrical three-up is an AI tell) carrying the wine pairing price as a heading and the allergy policy as a heading, each with one honest paragraph. Then a 'Find us' section above a 2px tan rule: address and seating times on the left, the phone number large in the slab face and a final solid cream 'Book a table' button on the right. Close with a single-line footer holding the wordmark, the street address and a copyright year.

special_ui_components.component: Seating picker that rewrites the menu, in pure CSS
special_ui_components.description: The whole point of view, and the thing worth copying: a selected option diffs a content list with no JavaScript at all.
special_ui_components.prompt: Put the radio inputs as SIBLINGS ahead of both the control row and the content they affect, so a general sibling combinator (~) can reach everything from any input. Hide them with an sr-only class and drive three things from `:checked`: the selected block's fill, which content rows are struck out, and any text that names the current selection. Keep one input `checked` in the markup so a static screenshot shows the mechanic already working, and never rely on `:hover` or JavaScript for the primary state. The pattern generalises to any list that changes with a chosen option: a menu by service, a schedule by day, a price table by plan, a spec sheet by model.

special_ui_components.component: Struck dish with its real reason printed beside it
special_ui_components.description: Unavailable content stays visible and says why, which is the opinion the design is holding.
special_ui_components.prompt: When a row is unavailable for the selected option, do not hide it and do not just grey it: strike the name and the price with a 2px line-through, drop both to the muted sage, dim the description, and reveal a solid sage TAG next to the name naming the constraint in plain words ('Late service only'). Keep the tag hidden by default with `display: none` and reveal it with the same `:checked ~` rule that applies the strike, so tag and strike can never disagree. Tie the constraint to a NAMED state rather than a clock time, because a printed time invites arithmetic against every other time on the page and a named service cannot contradict itself.

special_ui_components.component: Hatched, unselectable block for what is genuinely gone
special_ui_components.description: Losing availability costs a slot its fill and earns it the ugliest mark on the page.
special_ui_components.prompt: Fill the unavailable option's block with a 45-degree `repeating-linear-gradient` hatch in the muted accent over the dark fill, give it a matching border and `cursor: not-allowed`, mark its input `disabled` so it cannot be selected, and strike through its label. Set the numerals and the status word on small solid backings of the base fill so they stay legible through the hatch. Draw the hatch loud enough that it is the first thing the eye catches in the row.

special_ui_components.component: A control with real mass, not hairline chips
special_ui_components.description: Why the idea survives at library-grid size instead of reducing to a coloured rectangle.
special_ui_components.prompt: Draw the primary control as FILLED blocks with 2px borders and numerals at 44px, sized `flex: 1 1 150px` so they span the content width, and put them directly under a plain instruction heading rather than a decorative label. Keep the masthead deliberately small so the control, not the wordmark, is the heaviest object above the fold. An interactive point of view drawn in thin marks disappears at thumbnail size, and a selected state that is only a border colour disappears with it.

special_ui_components.description: The heading and the button both name the current selection, so the page never contradicts itself.
special_ui_components.prompt: Inside the section heading and inside the primary button, place one small `<span>` per option, all hidden by default, and reveal exactly the matching one with the same `:checked ~` rules that drive the rest of the state. The heading then reads 'Cooking at 20:00' and the button reads 'Book the 20:00 seating' with no scripting, and it is structurally impossible for either to name a different option than the one that is selected.

special_ui_components.component: One light band holding the brightest value
special_ui_components.description: How the primary action stays findable in grayscale on a dark page.
special_ui_components.prompt: Reserve the lightest colour in the palette for the primary buttons and exactly one full-width band, and let every other light element sit a step below it. Desaturate the finished page and check that the booking button is among the brightest objects on it. Avoid placing a large light-filled element immediately beside the primary button, or the two compete for the eye at a distance.
